extra.message: Hardcoded JWT secret key enables authentication bypass — An attacker can forge valid JWT tokens for any user role (including support_admin), gaining full access to the application, including all customer data, tickets, admin functions. [verified: No compensating control prevents use of the default 'dev-only-change-me-in-prod-...' secret_key. The hardcoded default is used as-is when the env variable is unset, allowing an attacker to forge JWTs for any user.]

Server-Side Template Injection in /ops/jinja endpoint — Remote code execution on the server, leading to full compromise of the application and underlying host. [verified: The endpoint at line 88 directly concatenates the user-supplied 'fragment' query parameter into a Jinja2 template string without any sanitization, enabling Server-Side Template Injection that can lead to remote code execution. The gate token does not neutralize the input; it only restricts access, making it exploitable by anyone with the token.]

Horizontal Privilege Escalation via Cross-Org Escalation Assignment — A customer can assign an escalation to any staff user in the system, potentially exposing ticket data to unauthorized personnel across organizations. [verified: In create_escalation (line 86-90), the assignee is validated only with is_staff() (line 89), not by organization membership. This allows a customer to assign an escalation to any staff user across organizations, enabling potential cross-org ticket exposure if the assignee has cross-org view permissions or through notification details.]

Path Traversal in /ops/vault endpoint leading to arbitrary file write — Arbitrary file write within application permissions, which can be leveraged for remote code execution (e.g., overwriting a Python module or configuration file) or data corruption. [verified: The `ref` parameter at line 55 is directly interpolated into the file path without any sanitization, allowing path traversal (e.g., `../../etc/passwd`). The gate token restricts access but does not neutralize the path traversal flaw; an attacker who obtains the token can exploit it.]

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in /ops/relay endpoint — Access to internal network services, cloud metadata (potentially exposing IAM credentials), and ability to scan internal infrastructure; may lead to lateral movement or data exfiltration. [verified: The `endpoint` query parameter is passed directly to `urllib.request.urlopen` without any validation or allowlisting. The only gate is `_wrk_gate` which authenticates the requester but does not restrict the target URL, allowing an authorized user to make arbitrary internal/external requests.]
